title: Microsoft Entra PowerShell Administration
scenario: NewVue Health is building administrative capability for cloud identity operations by using Microsoft Entra PowerShell. Before the organization moves into advanced identity lifecycle management and hybrid administration, the system administrator must prepare the workstation, install the correct module, connect securely to the tenant, and retrieve tenant, domain, user, and group data by using PowerShell. Because this is a complementary activity, use the case study and reference information below to complete the required tasks.

activities.title: Task 1 - Prepare the PowerShell Environment
activities.prompt: You want to prepare the workstation for Microsoft Entra PowerShell administration before any cloud identity commands are executed. To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
steps: Check whether the Microsoft.Entra module is already available
Set the execution policy to RemoteSigned for the current user
answer: Check whether the Microsoft.Entra module is already available
Set the execution policy to RemoteSigned for the current user
activities.explanation: The lab sequence prepares the shell, verifies prerequisites, updates package tooling, and then applies the recommended execution policy. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}

activities.title: Task 2 - Complete the Workstation Preparation Script
activities.prompt: You want to verify prerequisites and apply the recommended execution policy before installing the Microsoft Entra module. To answer, select the appropriate value for each blank in the script.
activities.explanation: The preparation phase uses `$PSVersionTable.PSVersion`, checks `Microsoft.Entra`, and sets `RemoteSigned` at the `CurrentUser` scope. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

activities.title: Task 3 - Install and Verify the Module
activities.prompt: You want to install the correct Microsoft Entra module and then verify that the module packages are available on the workstation. To answer, select the appropriate value for each blank in the script.
activities.explanation: The lab explicitly installs `Microsoft.Entra` from `PSGallery` for the `CurrentUser` scope and verifies with `Get-Module -ListAvailable Microsoft.Entra*`. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

activities.title: Task 4 - Connect to the Tenant
activities.prompt: You want to import the module, authenticate to the tenant, and verify the connected cloud context before running identity queries. To answer, select the appropriate value for each blank in the script.
activities.explanation: The lab sequence imports `Microsoft.Entra`, connects with `Connect-Entra -Scopes "User.Read.All","Directory.Read.All"`, and validates with `Get-EntraContext`. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

activities.title: Task 5 - Map the Query Commands
activities.prompt: You want to retrieve the correct identity data from the tenant after authentication is complete. To answer, match each command on the left with the information it returns on the right.
activities.explanation: These commands are the core retrieval commands used in the later stages of the lab. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}

activities.title: Task 6 - Query Users with Filtering and Formatting
activities.prompt: You want to return only the essential identity properties for cloud users and then perform a keyword search for administrative accounts. To answer, select the appropriate value for each blank in the script.
activities.explanation: The lab specifically uses `Select-Object DisplayName, UserPrincipalName` and a `-SearchString "admin"` filter. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

activities.title: Task 7 - Query Groups and Membership
activities.prompt: You want to retrieve group information and then review the membership of a specific group. To answer, select the appropriate value for each blank in the script.
activities.explanation: The lab ends by listing groups with `DisplayName` and `GroupType`, then retrieving members with `Get-EntraGroupMember -GroupId <GroupObjectId>`. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
